You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

svd2rust

Generate Rust register maps from SVD files.

This repository provides a tool that converts ARM CMSIS-SVD descriptions into source files that represent hardware peripheral registers and fields. The tool accepts an SVD file as input and produces register maps suitable for use in device support code.

Usage

  svd2rust [OPTIONS] <input.svd>

See the project documentation or the generated help output for available options and examples.

Generate a Rust API from SVD files

Usage: executable [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -i <FILE>
          Input SVD file

  -o, --output-dir <PATH>
          Directory to place generated files

  -c, --config <TOML_FILE>
          Config TOML file

      --settings <YAML_FILE>
          Target-specific settings YAML file

      --edition <YEAR>
          Rust edition of generated code

      --target <ARCH>
          Target architecture

      --atomics
          Generate atomic register modification API

      --atomics-feature <FEATURE>
          add feature gating for atomic register modification API

      --ignore-groups
          Don't add alternateGroup name as prefix to register name

      --keep-list
          Keep lists when generating code of dimElement, instead of trying to generate arrays

  -g, --generic-mod
          Push generic mod in separate file

      --feature-group
          Use group_name of peripherals as feature

      --feature-peripheral
          Use independent cfg feature flags for each peripheral

  -f, --ident-format <ident_format>
          Specify `-f type:prefix:case:suffix` to change default ident formatting.
          Allowed values of `type` are ["cluster_mod", "field_reader", "cluster_accessor", "peripheral", "enum_read_name", "enum_name", "register_accessor", "field_writer", "cluster", "register_spec", "peripheral_spec", "peripheral_mod", "interrupt", "enum_value", "enum_value_accessor", "register", "peripheral_feature", "field_accessor", "register_mod", "peripheral_singleton", "enum_write_name"].
          Allowed cases are `unchanged` (''), `pascal` ('p'), `constant` ('c') and `snake` ('s').
          

      --ident-formats-theme <THEME>
          A set of `ident_format` settings. `new` or `legacy`

      --field-names-for-enums
          Use field name for enumerations even when enumeratedValues has a name

      --max-cluster-size
          Use array increment for cluster size

      --impl-debug
          implement Debug for readable blocks and registers

      --impl-debug-feature <FEATURE>
          Add feature gating for block and register debug implementation

      --impl-defmt <FEATURE>
          Add automatic defmt implementation for enumerated values

  -m, --make-mod
          Create mod.rs instead of lib.rs, without inner attributes

      --skip-crate-attributes
          Do not generate crate attributes

  -s, --strict
          Make advanced checks due to parsing SVD

      --source-type <source_type>
          Specify file/stream format

      --reexport-core-peripherals
          For Cortex-M target reexport peripherals from cortex-m crate

      --reexport-interrupt
          Reexport interrupt macro from cortex-m-rt like crates

  -b, --base-address-shift <base_address_shift>
          Add offset to all base addresses on all peripherals in the SVD file.
          Useful for soft-cores where the peripheral address range isn't necessarily fixed.
          Ignore this option if you are not building your own FPGA based soft-cores.

  -l, --log <log_level>
          Choose which messages to log (overrides RUST_LOG)
          
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

    outdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    cmd = ['./executable', '-i', svd, '-o', outdir] + args
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    files = {}
    for p in pathlib.Path(outdir).glob('*'):
        files[p.name] = p.read_text()[:20000] if p.stat().st_size < 50000 else f"<large {p.stat().st_size}>"
    shutil.rmtree(outdir)
    return result, files

def test(name, args):
    result, files = run(args)
    print(f"=== {name} args={args} RC={result.returncode}")
    print("STDERR:", result.stderr[:1000].replace('\n',' | '))
    print("FILES:", list(files.keys()))
    for k,v in files.items():
        print(f"  {k}: len approx, preview: {v[:800].replace(chr(10),' ')}")
    print()

import subprocess, os, re
def get_help(arg):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.pop('RUST_LOG',None)
    m=subprocess.run(['python3','src/main.py',arg],capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
    o=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable',arg],capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
    # normalize prog and ident line
    m_out=m.stdout.replace('main.py','executable')
    # extract ident sets
    def normalize(s):
        lines=s.splitlines()
        for i,l in enumerate(lines):
            if 'Allowed values of `type`' in l:
                # sort idents
                idents=re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', l)
                idents_sorted=sorted(idents)
                lines[i]='          Allowed values of `type` are ["' + '", "'.join(idents_sorted) + '"].'
        return '\n'.join(lines)
    m_norm=normalize(m_out)
    o_norm=normalize(o.stdout)
    if m_norm==o_norm:
        print(arg, "MATCH")
    else:
        print(arg, "DIFF")
        import difflib
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(o_norm.splitlines(), m_norm.splitlines(), lineterm=''):
            print(line)
            if 'Allowed' in line:
                print("...")

get_help('--help')
get_help('-h')

    # Parse -f string like "type:prefix:case:suffix" with rules observed:
    # - Split by ":" (all parts, not limited). If 1 part (no colon), ignore (return None).
    # - If 2 parts: [type, case] (prefix/suffix empty). If type valid and case valid, return (type, "", case, "")? Else None.
    # - If 3 parts: [type, prefix, case] (suffix empty). If valid, return.
    # - If 4+ parts: [type, prefix, case, suffix, ...] (extra ignored, suffix is 4th part). If valid, return.
    # - Type must be one of IDENT_TYPES (case-sensitive, exact). Else None (ignore).
    # - Case must be one of: "", "snake", "pascal", "constant", "unchanged", "s", "p", "c" (lowercase, case-sensitive). Else None (ignore, fallback to default).
    #   - "" (empty) means unchanged (None).
    #   - "s"->Snake, "p"->Pascal, "c"->Constant, "snake"->Snake, etc., "unchanged"->None, ""->None.

    # - What about "peripheral :..." (type with trailing space)? "peripheral " != "peripheral", ignore. Good. (Observed ignored.)
    # Returns (type, prefix, case_normalized, suffix) or None if ignored.
    # case_normalized is "Pascal"/"Snake"/"Constant"/None
    if ":" not in s:
        return None
    parts = s.split(":")
    if len(parts) < 2:
        return None
    if len(parts) == 2:
        typ, case_raw = parts
        prefix = ""
        suffix = ""
        case_str = case_raw
    elif len(parts) == 3:
        typ, prefix, case_raw = parts
        suffix = ""
        case_str = case_raw
    else:  # 4+
        typ = parts[0]
        prefix = parts[1]
        case_raw = parts[2]
        suffix = parts[3]
        # extra parts parts[4:] ignored
        case_str = case_raw
    if typ not in IDENT_TYPES:
        return None
    # Validate case
    if case_str == "":
        case_norm = None
    elif case_str == "snake" or case_str == "s":
        case_norm = "Snake"
    elif case_str == "pascal" or case_str == "p":
        case_norm = "Pascal"
    elif case_str == "constant" or case_str == "c":
        case_norm = "Constant"
    elif case_str == "unchanged":
        case_norm = None
    else:
        return None
    return (typ, prefix, case_norm, suffix)

    # - Prefix/suffix can be any string (including empty, spaces? Spaces will cause invalid ident panic later, not ignored here). Even with spaces, return (don't ignore), let later panic.
    # - What about type with spaces like " peripheral" (leading space)? Type must match exactly, so " peripheral" (with space) != "peripheral", ignore. Good. (Observed " peripheral:..." ignored.)
    # - What about "peripheral :..." (type with trailing space)? "peripheral " != "peripheral", ignore. Good. (Observed ignored.)
    # Returns (type, prefix, case_normalized, suffix) or None if ignored.
    # case_normalized is "Pascal"/"Snake"/"Constant"/None
    if ":" not in s:
        return None
    parts = s.split(":")
    if len(parts) < 2:
        return None
    if len(parts) == 2:
        typ, case_raw = parts
        prefix = ""
        suffix = ""
        case_str = case_raw
    elif len(parts) == 3:
        typ, prefix, case_raw = parts
        suffix = ""
        case_str = case_raw
    else:  # 4+
        typ = parts[0]
        prefix = parts[1]
        case_raw = parts[2]
        suffix = parts[3]
        # extra parts parts[4:] ignored
        case_str = case_raw
    if typ not in IDENT_TYPES:
        return None
    # Validate case
    if case_str == "":
        case_norm = None
    elif case_str == "snake" or case_str == "s":
        case_norm = "Snake"
    elif case_str == "pascal" or case_str == "p":
        case_norm = "Pascal"
    elif case_str == "constant" or case_str == "c":
        case_norm = "Constant"
    elif case_str == "unchanged":
        case_norm = None
    else:
        return None
    return (typ, prefix, case_norm, suffix)

mod atomic {
    use super::*;
    use portable_atomic::Ordering;

    pub trait AtomicOperations {
        unsafe fn atomic_or(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self);
        unsafe fn atomic_and(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self);
        unsafe fn atomic_xor(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self);
    }

    macro_rules! impl_atomics {
        ($U:ty, $Atomic:ty) => {
            impl AtomicOperations for $U {
                unsafe fn atomic_or(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self) {
                    (*(ptr as *const $Atomic)).or(val, Ordering::SeqCst);
                }

                unsafe fn atomic_and(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self) {
                    (*(ptr as *const $Atomic)).and(val, Ordering::SeqCst);
                }

                unsafe fn atomic_xor(ptr: *mut Self, val: Self) {
                    (*(ptr as *const $Atomic)).xor(val, Ordering::SeqCst);
                }
            }
        };
    }

    impl_atomics!(u8, portable_atomic::AtomicU8);
    impl_atomics!(u16, portable_atomic::AtomicU16);

import subprocess, tempfile, pathlib, shutil
def get_interrupt_block(target, svd='/tmp/minimal.svd', edition='2021'):
    outdir=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    args=['-i',svd,'-o',outdir,'--target',target,'--edition',edition]
    subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable']+args,capture_output=True)
    lib=pathlib.Path(outdir+'/lib.rs').read_text()
    # Find generic end to peripheral start
    # Generic end: find 'impl < REG : Readable > core :: fmt :: Debug' + ... + ' } }' + '\n'?
    # Simpler: find start of interrupt (after generic) and end before peripheral
    # For minimal, peripheral starts at '#[doc = "Timer 0"] pub type Tim0'
    # For complex, peripheral starts at '#[doc = "GPIO Port A"] pub type Gpioa'
    # Generic end marker: 'core :: fmt :: Debug :: fmt (& self . read () , f) } } }' + '\n'?
    # Let's just extract between generic end and peripheral start by finding peripheral start and going back?
    # For 0 interrupts mips/none, there is no interrupt block, so generic end == peripheral start (no gap)? Actually for mips minimal, after generic '...} } }\n', next is '#[doc="Timer 0"]...', no interrupt. Good.
    # For cortex-m minimal, after generic, next is '#[cfg...] extern...', then vector, etc., then '#[doc="Timer 0"]...'.
    # To extract interrupt block, find generic end idx and peripheral start idx.
    gen_end_marker = "core :: fmt :: Debug :: fmt (& self . read () , f) } } }"
    gen_idx = lib.find(gen_end_marker)
    if gen_idx == -1:
        print(f"target {target} gen marker not found")
        shutil.rmtree(outdir)
        return None
    gen_end = gen_idx + len(gen_end_marker)
    # Find peripheral start: first occurrence of 'pub type' after gen_end? For minimal, 'pub type Tim0', for complex 'pub type Gpioa'
    # Actually peripheral block starts with '#[doc = "Timer 0"] pub type' or similar. Find 'pub type'?
    periph_idx = lib.find("pub type", gen_end)
    # Interrupt block is lib[gen_end:periph_idx] (includes leading \n and trailing?).
    block = lib[gen_end:periph_idx]
    shutil.rmtree(outdir)
    return block

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

class SvdError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, chain):
        # chain is list of strings, e.g., ["0: Parsing device `TEST` at 1:22", "1: ..."]
        # Or single message like "the document does not have a root node", "unknown token at 1:1", etc.
        self.chain = chain
        super().__init__("\n".join(chain))

def find_tag_line_col(content, tag, occurrence=0):
    # Find line/col of <tag in content (for error reporting). occurrence 0-based.
    # Search for f"<{tag}" (with < and tag, possibly with space or > after? For <device, <device>, <device ...>, etc.)
    # Return (line, col) 1-based. If not found, return (1,1)?
    # For device at 1:22 in '<?xml version="1.0"?><device...', find '<device' at index 21 (0-based), line 1 col 22. Good.
    idx = -1
    start = 0
    for _ in range(occurrence+1):
        idx = content.find(f"<{tag}", start)
        if idx == -1:
            return (1, 1)
        start = idx + 1
    # Compute line/col
    before = content[:idx]
    line = before.count("\n") + 1
    last_nl = before.rfind("\n")
    if last_nl == -1:
        col = idx + 1
    else:
        col = idx - last_nl
    return (line, col)

def get_child_text(elem, tag, default=None):
    child = elem.find(tag)
    if child is None:

    # Get text, strip? SVD text may contain whitespace/newlines? For descriptions, need to preserve? Actually descriptions with newlines are collapsed to single space later. For names, strip.
    # For empty tag <tag></tag> or <tag/> with no text, return ""? Or None? For baseAddress empty, error "Expected content..." (as observed for empty baseAddress). So need to distinguish None (no tag) vs "" (empty tag).
    # ET: <tag></tag> gives child.text None? Actually <tag></tag> with no content gives None. <tag>   </tag> with whitespace gives "   "? Hmm.

    txt = child.text
    if txt is None:
        # Check if has children? Unlikely for simple tags. Return ""?
        return ""
    return txt

def get_child_text_stripped(elem, tag, default=None):
    txt = get_child_text(elem, tag, default)

def gen_periph2(periph, device, idents, cfg):
    pname=periph.name
    ptype=apply_ident(pname,"peripheral",idents)
    pmod=apply_ident(pname,"peripheral_mod",idents)
    pspec=apply_ident(pname,"peripheral_spec",idents)
    base=periph.base_address+cfg.get("base_address_shift",0)
    bstr=format_address(base)
    pdesc=escape_doc_str(pname if not periph.description or not periph.description.strip() else periph.description)
    hu=cfg.get("html_url")
    extra=""
    if hu:
        bu=hu.rstrip("/")
        lk=f"{bu}/#{pname}"
        extra='\n#[doc = ""]\n#[doc = "See peripheral [structure]('+lk+')"]'
    hdr=f'#[doc = "{pdesc}"]{extra} pub type {ptype} = crate :: Periph < {pspec} > ; pub struct {pspec} ; impl crate :: PeripheralSpec for {pspec} {{ type RB = {pmod} :: RegisterBlock ; const ADDRESS : usize = {bstr} ; const NAME : & \'static str = "{ptype}" ; }}\n'
    ms=f'#[doc = "{pdesc}"] pub mod {pmod} {{\n'
    regs=sorted(periph.registers, key=lambda r: (r.address_offset, r.name))
    flds=[]; accs=[]; off=0
    for idx,reg in enumerate(regs):
        sz=reg.size if getattr(reg,"size",None) is not None else device.size
        sb=(sz+7)//8
        st=reg.address_offset
        if st>off:
            gap=st-off
            gs=format_hex(gap)
            flds.append(f"_reserved{idx} : [u8 ; {gs}] ,")
        rt=apply_ident(reg.name,"register",idents)
        ra=apply_ident(reg.name,"register_accessor",idents)
        flds.append(f"{ra} : {rt} ,")
        ostr=f"0x{st:02x}"
        rd=escape_doc_str(reg.name if not reg.description or not reg.description.strip() else reg.description)
        accs.append(f'#[doc = "{ostr} - {rd}"]\n#[inline (always)] pub const fn {ra} (& self) -> & {rt} {{ & self . {ra} }}')
        off=st+sb
    dbg=cfg.get("impl_debug",False)
    dbgf=cfg.get("impl_debug_feature")
    if dbg:
        da=f'#[cfg_attr (feature = "{dbgf}" , derive (Debug))]\n' if dbgf else '#[derive (Debug)]\n'
        rbh=f'#[repr (C)]\n{da}#[doc = "Register block"] pub struct RegisterBlock {{ '
    else:
        rbh='#[repr (C)]\n#[doc = "Register block"] pub struct RegisterBlock { '
    rbf=" ".join(flds)
    rbm="\n".join(accs)
    rbfull=f"{rbh}{rbf}}} impl RegisterBlock {{\n{rbm} }}\n"
    rcs=[]
    for reg in regs:
        rh,rb=gen_register(reg,device.size,idents,cfg)
        rcs.append(rh+rb+"}\n")
    rj="".join(rcs)
    return hdr+ms+rbfull+rj+"} "
